narrativeReportMd:
# SubstanceNucleicAcid R4->R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`SubstanceNucleicAcid` is a hard breaking change: the concrete R4 resource is absent from the R6 ballot package. R4 instances with `resourceType: "SubstanceNucleicAcid"` will not validate as R6 resources, and generated R6 models/servers are unlikely to expose a `SubstanceNucleicAcid` class or endpoint.

## Scope
I analyzed the R4 `SubstanceNucleicAcid` StructureDefinition, confirmed the assigned R6 file is absent, checked the R6 package index for an exact match, and inspected the only R6 Substance-family StructureDefinitions: `Substance` and `SubstanceDefinition`. `SubstanceDefinition` is the closest inferred successor, but it is a broader substance definition resource rather than a same-name replacement. Inherited `DomainResource`, `Resource`, `Element`, and `BackboneElement` changes are out of scope.

## Main migration themes
The key migration issue is not a narrow cardinality or terminology edit; it is replacement/removal of an entire draft resource. The R4 resource's nucleic-acid-specific fields such as `sequenceType`, `numberOfSubunits`, `areaOfHybridisation`, `oligoNucleotideType`, `subunit.sequence`, `subunit.linkage.*`, and `subunit.sugar.*` do not have same-path R6 elements. R6 `SubstanceDefinition` can classify a substance as nucleic acid and can carry generic structural representations or documents, but that is not a lossless structured mapping for the R4 subunit/linkage/sugar model.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact issue is the missing R6 artifact itself (`SubstanceNucleicAcid:ARTIFACT_IDENTITY:root:3f7c21`). A second high-impact issue is the loss of the R4 nucleic-acid-specific content model under the inferred successor (`SubstanceNucleicAcid:ELEMENT_PRESENCE_OR_IDENTITY:subunit:8b0a12`). Code generation and runtime dispatch are also high risk because R6 code generated from the ballot package will not contain the R4 resource type.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed for the intended migration from the R4 IDMP-style nucleic acid model to R6 `SubstanceDefinition`, especially where regulated substance data needs lossless preservation of subunit order, terminal residues, linkage connectivity, sugar identifiers, or sequence attachments.

## Backward-compatible design observations
A less disruptive design could have kept `SubstanceNucleicAcid` as deprecated or supplied an official cross-version profile/extension mapping while introducing `SubstanceDefinition`. The tradeoff would be maintaining duplicate substance models during a major-version cleanup.

## Follow-up analysis
Review R6 `SubstanceDefinition`, R6 `Substance`, and any official cross-version conversion maps or narrative change notes outside the local package to establish the intended, regulator-safe migration pattern.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `SubstanceNucleicAcid` is absent from the R6 ballot package, so R4 instances are directly invalid in R6. The top migration concerns are resource-type removal, loss of same-path structured nucleic-acid subunit/linkage/sugar fields, and generated-code/server endpoint removal. The main uncertainty is the official intended mapping to `SubstanceDefinition` because no local diff or ConceptMap was available.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should treat this as an artifact replacement/removal rather than a field-level edit. Existing R4 data needs an explicit transformation target, most plausibly `SubstanceDefinition` for substance master data and possibly `Substance` for material instances. Lossless migration requires decisions for R4 fields that have no direct R6 peer: subunit count/order, 5'-3' sequence assumptions, hybridisation areas, terminal nucleotides, linkage connectivity, registered linkage fragments, sugar identifiers, and residue sites.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the same R6 artifact is absent: both the assigned file path and exact package-index lookup are negative, and the R6 package contains only `Substance` and `SubstanceDefinition` among Substance-family StructureDefinitions. Confidence is medium for the precise successor mapping because the available inputs did not include an official diff, change note, or cross-version ConceptMap.

findings.title: R6 removes the concrete SubstanceNucleicAcid resource identity

oldState.summary: R4 defines a concrete draft resource named SubstanceNucleicAcid.

semanticText.definition: Nucleic acids are defined by three distinct elements: the base, sugar and linkage. Individual substance/moiety IDs will be created for each of these elements. The nucleotide sequence will be always entered in the 5'-3' direction.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 has a first-class `SubstanceNucleicAcid` resource with canonical URL `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/SubstanceNucleicAcid`, type `SubstanceNucleicAcid`, and base `DomainResource`.

newState.summary: No same-name R6 StructureDefinition exists; SubstanceDefinition is only an inferred broader successor candidate.
newState.narrativeMd: The R6 package has no `StructureDefinition-SubstanceNucleicAcid.json` and no package-index entry with id or canonical URL `SubstanceNucleicAcid`. The only R6 Substance-family StructureDefinitions are `Substance` and `SubstanceDefinition`.

facts.note: No exact R6 StructureDefinition was found.
Candidate inferred from R6 Substance-family definitions, not from an official local mapping.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same canonical/id is absent in R6. `SubstanceDefinition` is the best local candidate because its description covers detailed substance descriptions and its `classification` definition explicitly gives nucleic acid as an example; however, the local inputs do not prove an official rename.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation break. A valid R4 resource with `resourceType: "SubstanceNucleicAcid"` has no corresponding R6 resource definition, so strict R6 validators and parsers generated from the ballot package will reject or not recognize it. R6 data migrated into `SubstanceDefinition` also cannot round-trip to the original R4 resource type without an explicit conversion rule.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The resource is draft and likely uncommon, but it can carry regulated medicinal substance identity and structural data where silent loss or misclassification may have compliance impact.

justification.inferredGoal: Consolidate the R4 IDMP-style substance-specific resources into the broader R6 SubstanceDefinition model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain SubstanceNucleicAcid in base R6 as a deprecated transitional resource while introducing SubstanceDefinition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Consolidating the draft R4 IDMP-style substance resources into the broader `SubstanceDefinition` model is a reasonable inferred R6 goal, and a major-version ballot is a plausible place to remove obsolete core surface area. The break is still severe for adopters, but the main less-breaking base-design path would keep a deprecated resource beside its successor, which has material long-term interoperability and maintenance costs. Because no local change rationale or official conversion map was available, this is not assessed as fully justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest less-breaking base R6 design would be to keep the concrete `SubstanceNucleicAcid` resource in core as deprecated for a transition period, with definitions and guidance pointing implementers toward `SubstanceDefinition`. Ordinary conversion tooling, profiles, or extension packages would be useful mitigations but are not counted as the base-design alternative. Keeping the old resource would preserve `resourceType` and old paths, but it risks an indefinite legacy model and duplicate representations of the same substance definition.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve old instances, but would prolong duplicate substance models, endpoints, generated classes, and ambiguity about the preferred source of truth.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 example is intentionally minimal: `SubstanceNucleicAcid` has no local mandatory data elements. The R6 migration example is illustrative only and is not a lossless conversion.

findings.narrativeMd: The R4 artifact itself disappears in R6. This is more severe than a field rename because every instance, parser branch, generated class, REST type route, and profile that names `SubstanceNucleicAcid` loses its base resource type. `SubstanceDefinition` is a plausible successor for substance master data, but it is not a same-identity resource and cannot be accepted by systems expecting the R4 resource without transformation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid instance can become R6-invalid solely because of `resourceType`. Strict R6 validators will have no StructureDefinition to validate against, and generated parsers may treat the resource as unknown. Conversely, an R6 `SubstanceDefinition` that represents a nucleic acid cannot be represented as R4 `SubstanceNucleicAcid` without a deliberate transform that chooses how to populate the specialized R4 fields.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory all stored, exchanged, profiled, searched, or referenced `SubstanceNucleicAcid` resources. Decide whether each record is substance-definition data suitable for `SubstanceDefinition`, material-instance data suitable for `Substance`, or requires an extension/profile. Add tests that feed old `SubstanceNucleicAcid` instances to R6 validators and confirm the conversion pipeline either rejects them with a clear message or maps them explicitly.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Removal is likely part of a broader model cleanup, but a backward-compatible route could have retained the old resource as deprecated or supplied an official compatibility profile. Such a route would be less disruptive for validators and generated code, but would also prolong duplicate substance modeling and might undermine the intended R6 consolidation.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 defines `SubstanceNucleicAcid` as a concrete resource, while the R6 ballot package has no same-id StructureDefinition and appears to consolidate this area into broader `SubstanceDefinition` modeling. That is a real top-level break: even a minimal R4 instance with `resourceType: "SubstanceNucleicAcid"` has no direct R6 resource identity. Still, the removed artifact was FMM 0/trial-use, local evidence suggests this was a draft IDMP-style specialization, and the quick public-use check found IDMP testing/piloting rather than clear production use of this exact R4 resource. Keeping a deprecated resource would reduce breakage but would preserve duplicate substance identities and generated API surface in the base specification.

That would preserve most R4 instances and generated code, but at the cost of duplicate resource identities, endpoints, profile bases, and ambiguity about which substance model should be authoritative.

findings.title: R4 nucleic-acid-specific fields have no same-path R6 content model

oldState.summary: R4 has a dedicated nested content model for nucleic acid sequence, subunits, linkages, and sugars.
oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 differential defines local optional elements including `sequenceType`, `numberOfSubunits`, `areaOfHybridisation`, `oligoNucleotideType`, repeating `subunit`, `subunit.sequence`, `subunit.length`, `subunit.sequenceAttachment`, `subunit.fivePrime`, `subunit.threePrime`, repeating `subunit.linkage`, and repeating `subunit.sugar`.

newState.summary: The closest R6 candidate uses generic SubstanceDefinition classification and structure/representation fields, not the same specialized subunit/linkage/sugar paths.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `SubstanceDefinition` can classify the substance as nucleic acid and can carry generic structural representations or documents, but the inspected StructureDefinition has no local elements named `subunit`, `areaOfHybridisation`, `oligoNucleotideType`, `fivePrime`, `threePrime`, `linkage`, or `sugar`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The affected R4 paths are local differential elements under `SubstanceNucleicAcid`. The R6 candidate paths are selected because they are the only inspected `SubstanceDefinition` elements that can plausibly carry nucleic-acid classification or structure.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance containing these local fields is invalid as an R6 resource because the whole resource type is gone. Even after choosing `SubstanceDefinition` as a target, the R4 fields do not map one-to-one, so a naive converter will either drop data or serialize it into generic representations/extensions that R4 systems cannot interpret as the original structured elements.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: For implementations that used this artifact, subunit order, residue sites, sugar/linkage identifiers, and sequence attachments can be scientifically or regulatorily material.

justification.inferredGoal: Replace a specialized nucleic-acid model with a more generic substance-structure representation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Carry the R4 nucleic-acid subunit/linkage/sugar model forward as optional base R6 content, either on a deprecated SubstanceNucleicAcid resource or as structured optional content in SubstanceDefinition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: A generic `SubstanceDefinition.structure.representation` model is a reasonable simplification goal, but the local evidence does not show why R6 needed to drop all standardized structured nucleic-acid detail from the base design. The data at risk can be scientifically and regulatorily material, and the report's extension/profile/conversion-map options are mitigations rather than backwards-compatible base designs. A base alternative exists, but it has substantial duplication and complexity costs, so the availability is only partial.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base-design alternative would preserve the old structured facts as optional R6 content: for example, keep `SubstanceNucleicAcid` deprecated with its subunit/linkage/sugar paths, or add governed optional nucleic-acid structure backbones to `SubstanceDefinition`. That could preserve most R4 data while allowing generic representations for simpler cases. The tradeoff is material validation ambiguity: the same sequence, linkage, or sugar facts could appear in both generic representations and specialized fields, and deprecated representations may never fully disappear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Structured preservation would reduce data loss, but would make the generic substance model larger and create competing generic versus specialized encodings.

evidence.detail: R4 defines repeating subunits and descendant elements for sequence, length, sequenceAttachment, fivePrime, threePrime, linkage, and sugar.
R4 captures linkage connectivity/identifier/name/residueSite and sugar identifier/name/residueSite as structured sub-elements.
R6 candidate has generic classification and structure representation fields rather than same-path nucleic-acid subunit fields.
evidence.quote: A depiction of the structure of the substance.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example preserves only the sequence string and a broad classification; it does not preserve all R4 structured details such as subunit count, linkage identifier/name/residueSite, or sugar identifier/residueSite.

findings.narrativeMd: The old resource was not just a label for a substance; it encoded a nucleic-acid-specific structure. Losing the same-path fields affects systems that validated or queried `subunit.sequence`, counted subunits, distinguished linkage types, or represented sugar fragments with identifiers and residue sites. Mapping these into generic structure text is possible for some records but is not equivalent to preserving computable structured content.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with these fields are R6-invalid because the resource type is absent. If converted to `SubstanceDefinition`, the data can be made syntactically valid only by choosing a non-equivalent representation such as generic `structure.representation`, `structure.sourceDocument`, or extensions. R6-to-R4 round-trip is therefore high risk unless the migration retains original R4 semantics explicitly.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Build a field-by-field migration table before transforming production data. Preserve original values in standard cross-version extensions if available; otherwise use governed implementation-specific extensions and retain source documents for audit. Test at least: multiple subunits, identical repeated sequences, explicit non-3'-5' linkage connectivity, sequence attachments, and sugar residue sites.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This break could have been mitigated by keeping the old local elements as optional content in a profile or standard extension set. The generic model is simpler, but without a standardized bridge, implementers must invent mappings and may lose computable meaning.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review should decide whether a particular dataset can tolerate generic structural representation or requires a lossless extension/profile mapping.

freshReview.narrativeMd: At the affected path level, R4 had a structured nucleic-acid model for sequence type, subunit count, hybridisation area, oligonucleotide type, repeated subunits, sequence attachments, terminal residues, linkages, and sugars. The plausible R6 target, `SubstanceDefinition.structure.representation`, is generic text/document structure representation rather than a same-shape model. For an implementation that actually used this resource, migration is not just a property rename: subunit order, residue sites, sugar identifiers, linkage identifiers, and sequence attachments may require expert mapping or extensions. FMM 0 reduces the assumption of widespread deployment, but these fields are the core scientific/regulatory content of the resource, so dropping all standardized structured detail without a clear base bridge deserves renewed review.
keyEvidence: R4 differential defines optional local paths including `sequenceType`, `numberOfSubunits`, `areaOfHybridisation`, `oligoNucleotideType`, `subunit`, `subunit.sequence`, `subunit.sequenceAttachment`, `subunit.fivePrime`, `subunit.threePrime`, repeated `subunit.linkage`, and repeated `subunit.sugar`.
R4 linkage and sugar backbones include identifiers, names, and residue sites; linkage connectivity has its own structured field.
R6 `SubstanceDefinition.structure.representation` is defined as `A depiction of the structure of the substance` with representation string, format, and document fields.
R6 `SubstanceDefinition.classification` can classify a substance as nucleic acid, but the inspected R6 definition has no same-path subunit/linkage/sugar content model.
No local ConceptMap or StructureMap for `SubstanceNucleicAcid` to `SubstanceDefinition` was found in the R6 package index.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use softens broad adoption assumptions, so this is not Revisit merely because an element break exists. The concern remains because the affected fields are central to the artifact's purpose and can be scientifically or regulatorily material when the artifact is used.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: data can be made syntactically R6-valid only by mapping specialized R4 subunit/linkage/sugar structure into generic representation text, documents, or extensions, which loses computable same-path meaning unless a governed mapping is supplied.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A plausible less-breaking base design would either retain a deprecated `SubstanceNucleicAcid` resource for one transition period or add governed optional nucleic-acid structure backbones/extensions in base R6 `SubstanceDefinition`. The tradeoff is real: it makes the generic substance model larger and can create competing generic-versus-specialized encodings, but it would reduce expert-dependent data loss for the resource's core fields.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Partially agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment: the report correctly identifies material mapping loss and non-trivial tradeoffs, and the path-level centrality makes this worth revisiting despite low FMM.

findings.title: Generated R6 code and REST dispatch will not contain SubstanceNucleicAcid

oldState.summary: R4 code generators could produce a SubstanceNucleicAcid resource class/type and servers could expose resource-type-specific handling.
oldState.narrativeMd: Because R4 includes `SubstanceNucleicAcid` as a concrete resource StructureDefinition, generated SDKs, validators, serializers, and REST dispatch tables can include it as a known resource type.

newState.summary: R6 generators have no SubstanceNucleicAcid StructureDefinition to generate from.
newState.narrativeMd: An R6 build generated strictly from the ballot package will know `Substance` and `SubstanceDefinition`, but not `SubstanceNucleicAcid`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: This follows from the artifact identity removal: code generation over StructureDefinitions cannot create a resource class that has no R6 StructureDefinition.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Even before validation, applications commonly dispatch by `resourceType`, generated enum, class name, endpoint path, search parameter set, or profile base. All of those mechanisms can fail or require compatibility shims when the R6 artifact is absent.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Operational failures are likely limited to systems that adopted this draft resource, but such systems may be managing regulated substance definitions.

justification.inferredGoal: Remove obsolete generated surface area after consolidating substance modeling.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Avoid the codegen break only by retaining a deprecated core resource definition that R6 generators can still emit.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The runtime and code-generation break follows directly from accepting the core artifact removal. If R6's goal was to consolidate substance modeling and remove obsolete draft resource surface area, then dropping the generated class and REST type is probably justified. Compatibility SDKs or generated aliases are valuable migration mitigations, but they are not less-breaking base R6 designs unless the core package keeps a resource definition to generate from.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A base-design alternative would be to leave a deprecated `SubstanceNucleicAcid` StructureDefinition in R6 so generated validators, model libraries, resource-type enums, and REST dispatch tables still include it while warning implementers to migrate. A non-core cross-version library or converter would not count as the base alternative here. The cost is maintaining stale generated surface area and two runtime routes for substance-definition content.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would prevent enum/class/endpoint failures, but would keep legacy generated API surface and duplicate runtime paths in R6.

evidence.detail: No R6 StructureDefinition file exists for code generators to consume.
R6 has StructureDefinition-Substance.json and StructureDefinition-SubstanceDefinition.json only among Substance-family StructureDefinitions.

examples.examplesMd: A parser or REST layer that dispatches by `resourceType` has no R6 target class or endpoint for this fragment unless custom compatibility handling is added.

findings.narrativeMd: This is the application-level face of the resource removal. Code that compiles against an R4 generated `SubstanceNucleicAcid` class, switches over R4 resource-type enums, stores typed tables, or routes `/SubstanceNucleicAcid` REST requests will not migrate by simply regenerating from R6 definitions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: The break can appear as compile errors, unknown-resource parser results, failed deserialization, missing REST routes, or dropped typed search support. It is not a separate FHIR validation rule beyond the missing artifact, but it is a high-probability runtime migration failure for adopters.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Add a compatibility layer before moving to R6-generated classes. The layer should detect `SubstanceNucleicAcid`, invoke an explicit converter, and route migrated records to `SubstanceDefinition` or a governed extension/profile. Include regression tests for JSON parsing, resource-type enum handling, REST import/export, persistence schema, and any FHIRPath expressions that mention old paths.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A generated alias or legacy cross-version package would be less disruptive than complete absence in R6-generated code. The downside is that core R6 would still need a sanctioned place to document or host legacy conversions.

freshReview.narrativeMd: Generated R6 validators, model libraries, resource-type enums, and REST dispatch tables built strictly from the ballot package will not include `SubstanceNucleicAcid`. That is a genuine runtime/API/codegen break for systems that used the R4 resource type. However, this finding is the application-surface consequence of the same FMM 0 resource removal. If the base design goal is to remove draft specialized substance resources in favor of `SubstanceDefinition`, retaining a legacy class and endpoint in core R6 is the only true base-compatible alternative and has substantial maintenance and ambiguity costs.
keyEvidence: R4 package index includes `StructureDefinition-SubstanceNucleicAcid.json` as a concrete resource StructureDefinition.
R6 assigned StructureDefinition file for `SubstanceNucleicAcid` is absent.
R6 package index lists `StructureDefinition-Substance.json` and `StructureDefinition-SubstanceDefinition.json` as the Substance-family resource definitions, with no `SubstanceNucleicAcid` entry.
The break affects generated classes, known-resource dispatch, REST routes, and profile bases rather than adding a separate computable validation rule.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Low FMM and trial-use status lower the expected stability of generated API surface. Without clear evidence of production systems depending on the R4 generated type, this derivative runtime break appears proportionate to the resource cleanup.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: R6 generators have no StructureDefinition from which to emit a `SubstanceNucleicAcid` class, enum value, validator entry, search surface, or REST route.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: The less-breaking base option is the same as for the top-level removal: keep a deprecated R6 StructureDefinition so generators still emit the legacy surface. Compatibility libraries or converters help implementations but are not base R6 designs. The base option prevents codegen failures but prolongs stale generated APIs and duplicate runtime paths.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Partially agree with the existing High runtime impact and Partial alternative judgment: the runtime mechanism is accurately identified, but FMM 0 and its dependence on the accepted resource-removal decision make it probably acceptable.

findings.title: Nucleic-acid-specific conformance semantics are no longer expressed as a resource contract

oldState.summary: R4 embeds domain-specific assumptions in element definitions for nucleic acid representation.

semanticText.definition: The resource states that nucleotide sequence is entered in the 5'-3' direction, numberOfSubunits defaults to an assumption of 1 if unspecified, subunits are ordered by decreasing length and molecular weight, and linkage connectivity is assumed to be 3'-5' unless otherwise specified.

oldState.narrativeMd: These semantics live in the R4 StructureDefinition text and can guide validation, UI labels, authoring rules, and business interpretation even where there are no formal invariants.

newState.summary: The inferred R6 target is generic and does not carry these nucleic-acid-specific assumptions as same-scope conformance text.

semanticText.definition: R6 SubstanceDefinition provides broad classification and structural representation fields but not the same resource-level rules for sequence direction, default subunit count, subunit ordering, or linkage connectivity.

newState.narrativeMd: `SubstanceDefinition.classification` can say the substance is a nucleic acid, but the inspected R6 candidate does not encode the R4 conformance assumptions that made the specialized resource interpretable.

facts.newValue: not expressed in same-scope R6 candidate
not expressed in same-scope R6 candidate

facts.oldValue: decreasing length, then molecular weight; identical sequences repeated
facts.newValue: not expressed in same-scope R6 candidate
not expressed in same-scope R6 candidate

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old semantic statements are present in R4 local element definitions. The R6 candidate has generic structure text, so the comparison is semantic rather than a same-element text diff.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The semantics are not formal cardinality or invariant constraints, so this is not an additional hard validation break beyond artifact removal. It is still material because conversions that preserve only generic structure text may change business interpretation of missing subunit count, sequence orientation, ordering, and linkage defaults.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect sequence orientation or linkage assumptions can change scientific interpretation of a nucleic-acid substance.

justification.inferredGoal: Move detailed nucleic-acid semantics out of the base resource model or into generic substance structure representations.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain conditional nucleic-acid interpretation rules in base R6 SubstanceDefinition structure/representation definitions.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving to a generic substance-definition resource is reasonable, but losing the old 5-prime-to-3-prime, default subunit count, subunit ordering, and linkage-default semantics appears avoidable. Unlike preserving every old element, retaining these assumptions as conditional base conformance text or representation-format guidance would not substantially duplicate the data model. The supplied evidence does not show why R6 needed to omit that interpretive bridge.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design would add conditional text to `SubstanceDefinition.structure` or `SubstanceDefinition.structure.representation` stating how nucleic-acid sequence representations should be interpreted, including sequence direction, omitted subunit count, subunit ordering, and default linkage connectivity. A profile or conversion guide would also help implementers, but the counted alternative is the low-cost base R6 text/guidance itself.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This has low structural cost, but adds subtype-specific guidance to a generic resource and may not cover every regulated migration case.

evidence.detail: R4 root description states nucleic acid sequence direction and the base/sugar/linkage model.
evidence.quote: The nucleotide sequence will be always entered in the 5'-3' direction.

evidence.detail: R4 states that if numberOfSubunits is not specified, the assumption is 1 subunit.
R4 states linkage connectivity is assumed 3'-5' unless 3'-3' or 5'-5' is specified.
R6 SubstanceDefinition provides generic structural information and representation fields, not these nucleic-acid-specific assumptions.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 fragment can carry a sequence-like representation, but without agreed semantics it does not state whether the old R4 5'-3' and subunit/linkage assumptions apply.

findings.narrativeMd: Some of the most important R4 content was conveyed as definitional text rather than formal invariants. Removing the specialized resource removes the contract that a nucleotide sequence is in a specific orientation, that omitted subunit count implies one subunit, and that linkage connectivity has a default interpretation. Those assumptions may be invisible to generic R6 processors.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not a standalone old-valid/new-invalid rule because the hard validation break is already caused by artifact removal. The compatibility issue is semantic: data that can be serialized into an R6 generic representation may still be behaviorally different if downstream systems no longer apply the R4 nucleic-acid assumptions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Document semantic assumptions in the migration specification, not just in code. If using `SubstanceDefinition.structure.representation`, include representation format, orientation, and linkage assumptions explicitly or by reference to a profile. Review records where `numberOfSubunits` is omitted, where subunit order matters, or where linkage connectivity is not the default.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A profile or official conversion guide could preserve these semantics without restoring the full R4 resource. That would be a relatively compatible alternative because it keeps the R6 core generic while protecting implementers from divergent interpretations.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The impact depends heavily on whether an external R6 implementation guide exists for nucleic-acid substances; none was supplied in the local inputs.

freshReview.narrativeMd: This is not a standalone hard validation break; the structural break comes from the missing resource. The specific concern is semantic: R4 text defined the sequence direction, subunit default assumption, subunit ordering, and default linkage connectivity, while the inspected R6 `SubstanceDefinition` structure representation is generic and does not carry the same nucleic-acid-specific interpretation rules. For converted data, a bare representation string can be syntactically valid but semantically ambiguous. Because retaining at least conditional interpretation guidance in R6 would be a relatively low structural-cost bridge compared with restoring the whole resource, this omission deserves review even though low FMM limits the presumed deployment burden.
keyEvidence: R4 root description says nucleotide sequence is entered in the 5'-3' direction.
R4 `numberOfSubunits` definition says that if it is not specified, the assumption is one subunit.
R4 `subunit` definition states ordering by decreasing length and molecular weight, with identical sequences repeated.
R4 `subunit.linkage.connectivity` definition says connectivity is assumed 3'-5' unless 3'-3' or 5'-5' is specified.

R6 `SubstanceDefinition.structure.representation.representation` is only `The structural representation as a text string in a standard format`; R6 representation format codes inspected were InChI, SMILES, MOLFILE, CDX, SDF, PDB, and mmCIF.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use status prevents treating the semantic gap as broad production risk by default. It does not erase the concern because the old text governed the meaning of the resource's core sequence data, and the less-breaking bridge would be mostly definitional guidance rather than a large structural compatibility burden.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: converted R6 data may remain structurally valid but lose the R4 assumptions needed to interpret orientation, omitted subunit count, ordering, and linkage defaults.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could add conditional guidance to `SubstanceDefinition.structure` or `structure.representation` for nucleic-acid representations, or define a standard representation format/profile note that preserves the R4 assumptions. This has low structural cost, though it adds subtype-specific guidance to a generic resource and may not cover every detailed regulatory mapping case.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: Partially agree with the existing Medium impact and Yes alternative judgment: the concern is semantic rather than independently hard-breaking, but the proposed guidance-style alternative is plausible enough to merit renewed standards attention.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: No like-for-like R6 cardinality comparison is possible because the same artifact is absent. Within R4's local differential, all substantive `SubstanceNucleicAcid` data elements are optional (`0..1` or `0..*`), so no separate local minimum-cardinality strengthening was found beyond complete artifact removal.

R4 local element types were reviewed: CodeableConcept, integer, string, Attachment, Identifier, and BackboneElement. No independent choice-type narrowing or type replacement can be reported because there is no same-path R6 artifact; type risk is captured under removal and successor-mapping findings.

The R4 `SubstanceNucleicAcid` local differential contains no local Reference-typed data elements, so no local reference-target narrowing or widening was found. Inherited references and R6 candidate references are outside this local comparison.

R4 local CodeableConcept elements such as `sequenceType`, `oligoNucleotideType`, `fivePrime`, and `threePrime` have no local terminology binding in the R4 StructureDefinition. R6 `SubstanceDefinition` has several optional example/preferred/required bindings, but they are not same-path replacements for these R4 elements.

No local R4 differential invariants were found for `SubstanceNucleicAcid` elements. Snapshot constraints present on root and backbone elements are inherited base-artifact constraints and are excluded by scope.
No fixed, pattern, or defaultValue constraints were found on local R4 `SubstanceNucleicAcid` elements.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex constraints were found for the R4 artifact's own elements.
No local non-inherited `SubstanceNucleicAcid` data element was marked as a modifier. `implicitRules` and `modifierExtension` behavior is inherited from base artifacts and excluded.
No local slicing definitions were found on R4 `SubstanceNucleicAcid` elements.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 SubstanceDefinition explicitly allows nucleic acid as a classification example
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is not a direct breaking change to `SubstanceNucleicAcid` because it belongs to an inferred successor artifact, not a same-identity replacement. It is useful migration evidence because the R6 classification definition lists nucleic acid as an example.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Migration can use `SubstanceDefinition.classification` to mark a converted record as nucleic acid, but that does not preserve the R4 structured sequence/subunit/linkage/sugar content by itself.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 SubstanceDefinition provides generic structure representation fields
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The addition/existence of generic representation fields is not itself breaking; it is a possible migration target. The breaking issue is that these fields are not a lossless same-path replacement for R4 `SubstanceNucleicAcid`.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Use `structure.representation.representation`, `structure.representation.format`, and `structure.representation.document` for standard molecular/sequence representations only when the chosen format can carry the required detail. Otherwise preserve original R4 fields in extensions or source documents.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 Substance can reference SubstanceDefinition through Substance.code
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is not a direct change to `SubstanceNucleicAcid`; it is related migration context. R6 `Substance` remains a material substance resource and its required `code` is a CodeableReference to `SubstanceDefinition`.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: If an R4 `SubstanceNucleicAcid` record represented a definition/master-data concept, `SubstanceDefinition` is probably the target. If it represented an actual homogeneous material instance, a separate `Substance` instance referencing a `SubstanceDefinition` may be needed.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `SubstanceDefinition` is the closest inferred R6 successor and should have its own detailed R4/R6 assessment and migration guidance, including whether it intentionally subsumes R4 `SubstanceNucleicAcid`.
R6 `Substance` may be needed alongside `SubstanceDefinition` when old records are material instances rather than substance master definitions.
